questions.question_text: When a machine worth Rs. 5,00,000 is purchased for cash, what is the correct journal entry based on the Golden Rules of Accounting?

options.A: Debit: Cash; Credit: Machine
options.B: Debit: Machine; Credit: Cash
options.C: Debit: Machine; Credit: Bank Loan
options.D: Debit: Expense; Credit: Cash

questions.explanation: According to the Real Account rule 'Debit what comes in, Credit what goes out', the Machine (asset) comes in and is debited, while Cash (asset) goes out and is credited.

questions.question_text: A business sold goods worth Rs. 9,000 for Rs. 12,000 on credit to Mr. X. Which of the following correctly describes the impact on the accounting equation?

options.A: Sales +12,000; Mr. X +12,000; Goods -9,000; Cost of Sales -9,000
options.B: Sales +12,000; Mr. X -12,000; Goods -9,000; Cost of Sales +9,000
options.C: Sales -12,000; Mr. X +12,000; Goods +9,000; Cost of Sales -9,000
options.D: Sales +9,000; Mr. X +9,000; Goods -12,000; Cost of Sales -12,000

questions.explanation: Revenue (Sales) increases equity by 12,000, Debtors (Mr. X) increase assets by 12,000, Inventory (Goods) decreases assets by 9,000, and Cost of Sales reduces equity by 9,000.

questions.question_text: On 1st March 2024, a company took a loan from SBI for Rs. 1,00,000. What is the correct journal entry to record this transaction?

options.A: Debit: Loan Account; Credit: Cash and Bank
options.B: Debit: Interest Account; Credit: SBI Account
options.C: Debit: Cash and Bank; Credit: Loan Account
options.D: Debit: SBI Account; Credit: Interest Account

questions.explanation: When taking a loan, the asset (Cash/Bank) increases and is debited, while the liability (Loan) increases and is credited.

questions.question_text: What is the correct journal entry to record an outstanding water supply expense of Rs. 5,000 at year-end?

options.A: Debit: Water Supply Expense; Credit: Cash
options.B: Debit: Outstanding Water Supply Expense; Credit: Bank
options.C: Debit: Water Supply Expense; Credit: Outstanding Water Supply Expense
options.D: Debit: Outstanding Water Supply Expense; Credit: Water Supply Expense

questions.explanation: To record an outstanding expense, the Expense account is debited (increasing expenses) and the Outstanding Expense (a liability) is credited.

questions.question_text: When the proprietor introduces additional capital into the business in the form of cash, which accounts are affected?

options.A: Debit: Capital A/c; Credit: Cash A/c
options.B: Debit: Cash A/c; Credit: Drawings A/c
options.C: Debit: Cash A/c; Credit: Capital A/c
options.D: Debit: Bank A/c; Credit: Cash A/c

questions.explanation: Capital introduction increases the asset 'Cash' (Debit) and increases the 'Capital' liability/equity account (Credit).

questions.question_text: If a partner withdraws goods from the business for personal use, what is the correct credit entry?

options.A: Credit: Sales A/c
options.B: Credit: Purchases A/c
options.C: Credit: Capital A/c
options.D: Credit: Inventory on Consignment A/c

questions.explanation: When goods are taken for personal use (Drawings), the Drawings account is debited and the Purchases account is credited to reduce the cost of goods available for sale.

questions.question_text: Purchasing goods on credit from a supplier results in:

options.A: Decrease in Asset and Increase in Liability
options.B: Increase in Expense and Increase in Liability
options.C: Increase in Asset and Decrease in Capital
options.D: Decrease in Expense and Increase in Asset

questions.explanation: Purchases (Expense) increase and the Supplier (Liability) increases.

questions.question_text: What is the accounting entry for collecting cash from a debtor (customer)?

options.A: Debit: Customer A/c; Credit: Cash A/c
options.B: Debit: Cash A/c; Credit: Sales A/c
options.C: Debit: Cash A/c; Credit: Customer A/c
options.D: Debit: Bank A/c; Credit: Bad Debts A/c

questions.explanation: Collecting cash increases the asset 'Cash' (Debit) and decreases the asset 'Customer/Debtor' (Credit).

questions.question_text: How does a 'Prepaid Expense' adjustment affect the accounting equation?

options.A: Asset (+), Expense (-), Capital (+)
options.B: Asset (-), Expense (+), Capital (-)
options.C: Liability (+), Expense (+), Capital (-)
options.D: Asset (+), Liability (+), Capital (0)

questions.explanation: Prepaid expense creates an asset (+), reduces the current period's expense (-), which in turn increases capital (+).

questions.question_text: The journal entry for 'Accrued Interest Income' is:

options.A: Debit: Interest Income A/c; Credit: Interest Accrued A/c
options.B: Debit: Cash A/c; Credit: Interest Income A/c
options.C: Debit: Interest Accrued A/c; Credit: Interest Income A/c
options.D: Debit: Interest Accrued A/c; Credit: Cash A/c

questions.explanation: Accrued income is earned but not yet received. We debit the asset 'Interest Accrued' and credit the revenue 'Interest Income'.

questions.question_text: When raw materials are consumed in production, which account is credited?

options.A: Consumption Expense A/c
options.B: Inventory A/c
options.C: Purchases A/c
options.D: Work-in-Progress A/c

questions.explanation: Material consumption moves value from the asset (Inventory) to an expense (Consumption Expense). Therefore, Inventory is credited.

questions.question_text: What is the correct journal entry to record Depreciation Expense?

options.A: Debit: Asset A/c; Credit: Depreciation Expense A/c
options.B: Debit: Depreciation Expense A/c; Credit: Accumulated Depreciation A/c
options.C: Debit: Accumulated Depreciation A/c; Credit: Depreciation Expense A/c
options.D: Debit: Depreciation Expense A/c; Credit: Cash A/c

questions.explanation: Depreciation is an expense (Debit) and it increases the contra-asset account Accumulated Depreciation (Credit).

questions.question_text: Creating a 'Provision for Bad Debts' involves:

options.A: Debit: Provision for D.D.; Credit: Bad Debts Expense
options.B: Debit: Bad Debts Expense; Credit: Provision for D.D.
options.C: Debit: Customer A/c; Credit: Provision for D.D.
options.D: Debit: Cash A/c; Credit: Bad Debts Expense

questions.explanation: To create a provision, we recognize an expense (Debit) and increase the provision account (Credit).

questions.question_text: When a specific Bad Debt is written off against an existing provision, the entry is:

options.A: Debit: Bad Debts Expense; Credit: Customer A/c
options.B: Debit: Provision for D.D.; Credit: Customer A/c
options.C: Debit: Customer A/c; Credit: Provision for D.D.
options.D: Debit: Provision for D.D.; Credit: Bad Debts Expense

questions.explanation: Writing off against a provision reduces the provision (Debit) and reduces the customer's balance (Credit).

questions.question_text: What is the accounting impact of creating a Provision for Warranty?

options.A: Expense (+), Liability (+), Capital (-)
options.B: Expense (-), Liability (-), Capital (+)
options.C: Asset (+), Expense (+), Capital (-)
options.D: Asset (-), Liability (+), Capital (-)

questions.explanation: Creating a provision increases an expense and a liability, which reduces the overall capital.

questions.question_text: When a company utilizes a warranty provision to replace a defective part from inventory, it should:

options.A: Debit: Warranty Expense; Credit: Inventory
options.B: Debit: Provision for Warranty; Credit: Inventory
options.C: Debit: Inventory; Credit: Provision for Warranty
options.D: Debit: Cash; Credit: Provision for Warranty

questions.explanation: Utilization of a provision reduces the liability (Debit: Provision) and reduces the asset used (Credit: Inventory).

questions.question_text: Purchasing an asset on credit from a vendor results in:

options.A: Debit: Asset A/c; Credit: Cash A/c
options.B: Debit: Vendor A/c; Credit: Asset A/c
options.C: Debit: Asset A/c; Credit: Vendor A/c
options.D: Debit: Expense A/c; Credit: Vendor A/c

questions.explanation: The asset increases (Debit) and the liability to the vendor increases (Credit).

questions.question_text: When an asset is sold at a loss, which of the following is part of the journal entry?

options.A: Credit: Loss A/c
options.B: Debit: Asset A/c
options.C: Debit: Loss A/c
options.D: Credit: Accumulated Depreciation A/c

questions.explanation: A loss is an expense/reduction in equity and must be debited.

questions.question_text: In an asset exchange where an old asset and cash are given for a new asset, the new asset is:

options.A: Credited
options.B: Debited
options.C: Ignored
options.D: Recorded as a Liability

questions.explanation: The new asset 'comes in' to the business and is therefore debited.

questions.question_text: When goods are sent on consignment, the entry is:

options.A: Debit: Inventory A/c; Credit: Inventory on Consignment A/c
options.B: Debit: Inventory on Consignment A/c; Credit: Inventory A/c
options.C: Debit: Sales A/c; Credit: Inventory A/c
options.D: Debit: Consignee A/c; Credit: Sales A/c

questions.explanation: Goods are moved from general inventory to a specific consignment inventory account (both are assets).

questions.question_text: The entry to record the 'Cost of Sales' for goods sold on consignment is:

options.A: Debit: Cost of Sales A/c; Credit: Inventory on Consignment A/c
options.B: Debit: Inventory on Consignment A/c; Credit: Cost of Sales A/c
options.C: Debit: Sales A/c; Credit: Inventory A/c
options.D: Debit: Purchases A/c; Credit: Inventory on Consignment A/c

questions.explanation: Cost of Sales (Expense) is debited and the specific asset (Inventory on Consignment) is credited.

questions.question_text: When a new partner brings goodwill into the business, the 'Goodwill A/c' is debited and which account is credited?

options.A: New Partner's Capital A/c
options.B: Old Partners' Capital A/c
options.C: Cash A/c
options.D: Revaluation A/c

questions.explanation: Goodwill recognized upon admission of a partner is credited to the existing (old) partners' capital accounts.

questions.question_text: The issue of 'Bonus Shares' from reserves results in:

options.A: Increase in Total Assets
options.B: Decrease in Total Liabilities
options.C: Decrease in Reserves and Increase in Share Capital
options.D: Increase in Cash and Increase in Share Capital

questions.explanation: Bonus shares are a capitalization of reserves; Reserves (Debit/Decrease) and Share Capital (Credit/Increase).

questions.question_text: What is the journal entry for 'Share Forfeiture'?

options.A: Debit: Share Capital A/c; Credit: Forfeited Shares A/c
options.B: Debit: Forfeited Shares A/c; Credit: Share Capital A/c
options.C: Debit: Bank A/c; Credit: Share Capital A/c
options.D: Debit: Share Capital A/c; Credit: Bank A/c

questions.explanation: When shares are forfeited, the Share Capital is reduced (Debit) and the amount already received is moved to the Forfeited Shares account (Credit).

questions.question_text: When a company pays a salary to an employee in cash, the accounting impact is:

options.A: Asset (-), Expense (+), Capital (-)
options.B: Asset (+), Expense (+), Capital (+)
options.C: Asset (-), Liability (-), Capital (0)
options.D: Asset (+), Liability (+), Capital (-)

questions.explanation: Cash (Asset) decreases, Salary (Expense) increases, and because expenses reduce profit, Capital also decreases.
